interview.hardest_part: Building reliable mining, smelting, power, and red-science automation through precise screenshot-based inventory and placement actions, while also defending against Death world biters and paying Marathon's higher recipe and research costs.
interview.likely_failure: Most likely I will either lose too much time to crafting, fueling, and GUI/placement mistakes, or suffer an unrecoverable biter attack or character death before production becomes self-sustaining. A late stall before powered laboratories and sustained science consumption is also likely.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Planning occurs while paused, and the score rewards incremental production rather than requiring a rocket launch. Hand mining and handcrafting can earn early milestones, batch crafting reduces input overhead, and the starting burner drill and stone furnace can bootstrap automated iron without an electrical network. Burner machines, hand-fed furnaces, and manually crafted red science provide simple fallback strategies.
interview.harmful_mechanics: The three-hour wall-clock budget includes thinking and rendering, while each turn permits only one short input. Death world brings early, aggressive attacks amplified by pollution, Marathon increases costs and slows research, and native character death ends the only attempt. Continuous simulation, limited visual precision, fuel logistics, and the large 1000-item and 200-science requirements make the final milestones especially difficult.
